extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, filing, and prosecuting U.S. provisional and nonprovisional patent applications (content, form, filing-date rules, IDS handling, drawings, oaths/declarations, and related procedural matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory components of an application (35 U.S.C. 111)
rubrics_metrics.description: Such application shall include— (A) a specification as prescribed by section 112; (B) a drawing as prescribed by section 113; and (C) an oath or declaration as prescribed by section 115.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date is the date the specification, with or without claims, is received. The fee, oath or declaration, and 1 or more claims may be submitted after the filing date within a prescribed period and under conditions (including surcharge); failure to submit them within the prescribed period results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application content and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application must include a specification as prescribed by section 112(a) and a drawing as prescribed by section 113; a claim is not required in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete provisional application must include the cover sheet required by § 1.51(c)(1) (or ADS) identifying it as provisional and providing inventor name(s), residence, title, attorney/agent name and reg. no., docket, correspondence address, and government contract info if applicable. Provisional applications are regarded as abandoned 12 months after filing if not converted or relied upon, are not entitled to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119/365/386, and no IDS may be filed in a provisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For design patents (except continued prosecution), the filing date is when the specification (including at least one claim) and any required drawings are received. No new matter may be introduced after the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application under 37 CFR 1.51
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application (filed under §1.53(b) or (d)) comprises: (1) a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112, including claims; (2) the inventor’s oath or declaration; (3) drawings, when necessary; and (4) the prescribed filing, search, examination, and application size fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete provisional application under §1.53(c) comprises a cover sheet (per §1.51(c)(1)), a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a), drawings when necessary, and prescribed fees. Applicants are encouraged to file an IDS in nonprovisional applications but not in provisionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and contents of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred order: (A) Title; (B) Cross-reference to related applications; (C) Statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; (D) Names of parties to joint research agreement; (E) Incorporation by reference statements; (F) Statement regarding prior disclosures by inventor; (G) Background of the invention (field and related art); (H) Brief summary of the invention; (I) Brief description of the drawings; (J) Detailed description of the invention; (K) Claim(s) (commencing on a separate sheet); (L) Abstract of the disclosure (commencing on a separate sheet); (M) Sequence Listing if present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are suggested headers (upper case, without underlining/bold). If an Application Data Sheet (ADS) is used, data in the ADS need not be repeated elsewhere (with limited exceptions). See MPEP §608.01(a) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications must include at least one claim (as prescribed by subsections of section 112); provisional applications need not include a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a nonprovisional application initially lacks a claim, the applicant will be notified and given time to file claims or risk abandonment. Claims must be filed within the prescribed period or the application may be regarded as abandoned unless delay is shown to be unavoidable or unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing applications may only disclose and claim subject matter disclosed in the prior application. New matter by preliminary amendment and review of examiner’s holding of new matter are governed by MPEP §§ relating to new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: when required and acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required 'when necessary' and must be as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 113; drawings must be acceptable, located properly, and provide complete illustration where needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers new drawings when replacement required before examination, acceptability criteria, location of drawings, completeness and consistency checks by examiner, modifications in drawings, illustration of prior art, replacement drawings, transfer of drawings from prior applications, and which drawing changes require annotated sheets vs. which may be made without applicant-annotated sheets. See MPEP §608.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths and declarations and inventor naming
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor’s oath or declaration is required (per 35 U.S.C. 115) and the application must name the inventor(s); corrections to inventorship and ordering are subject to correction procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules cover inventor’s oath/declaration for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 and before, corrections of inventorship (requests and procedures), foreign executed oaths, oaths in continuing applications, supplemental oaths/declarations, and substitute statements. See MPEP §602 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) controls bibliographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Application Data Sheet is used, data supplied in the ADS need not be provided elsewhere in the application (with limited exceptions); the ADS will control where discrepancies exist except for inventor naming governed by 37 CFR 1.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, inventor citizenship must still be in the oath/declaration even if ADS contains it. See MPEP §601.05 and 37 CFR 1.76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet requirements for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application must include a cover sheet stating it is provisional and must identify the inventor(s), residence, title of the invention, attorney/agent name and reg. no. (if applicable), docket number (if applicable), correspondence address, and government agency/contract number if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet may be an ADS (§1.76) or a cover letter identifying the application as provisional; otherwise the filing will be treated as a nonprovisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under subsection (a) may be treated as a provisional application and vice versa under prescribed conditions, payment of fees, and within specified time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion of a provisional to nonprovisional requires fee set forth in §1.17(i) and an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (unless provisional already contains at least one such claim). Converting a provisional to nonprovisional can result in the patent term being measured from at least the provisional filing date; applicants should consider claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) instead of conversion to avoid adverse patent term impact. Deadlines for conversion are strict (e.g., before 12-month expiration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to meet filing date requirements and cure opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application does not meet filing requirements to be entitled to a filing date, the applicant will be notified (if correspondence address provided) and given a period to correct the filing error; failure to correct may lead to termination of proceedings and possible disposal with partial fee refund less handling fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under relevant CFR sections (with fees) may be required for review of notifications. In absence of timely petition, filing date will be the date the filing error is corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of application subsequent to filing (missing fees/claims/oath)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date lacks basic filing, search, or examination fees, at least one claim, or inventor's oath/declaration, the applicant will be notified and given time to supply these to avoid abandonment; timing differs if applicant provided correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions allow postponement of inventor's oath until issue fee date when certain ADS and identification criteria are met. Specific periods are set forth in §1.53(f)(1)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A continued prosecution (nonprovisional) application (continuation or divisional) may be filed under conditions: identify the prior application; disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior application; name same inventors (with limited exceptions); include request that it utilize the prior application's file jacket and contents to constitute the new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continued prosecution application uses the prior application's number for identification, may waive confidentiality to extent of file access, must be filed before payment of issue fee/abandonment/termination of prior proceedings, and may not introduce new matter. See §1.53(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Models, exhibits, and specimens generally excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: A model, exhibit, or specimen is normally not admitted as part of the application, although it may be required in prosecution (37 CFR 1.91 and 1.93, MPEP §608.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling rules and possible admission/return procedures are described in the referenced sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings, large tables, and program listings submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: “Sequence Listing,” “Large Tables,” or “Computer Program Listing Appendix” may be submitted in ASCII plain text or a 'Sequence Listing XML' in compliance with §§1.831-1.834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitted as PDF image files or on physical sheets, additional rules apply (see 37 CFR 1.821(c)(2)(3) and MPEP). Incorporation by reference of such files and allowable media (including read-only optical discs in limited situations) are governed by 37 CFR 1.52(e)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) content and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must comply with content requirements of 37 CFR 1.98 and timing requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 to be considered by the examiner; examiners use an IDS checklist to determine compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complying IDS will be considered by the examiner in the same manner as other documents in Office search files. Noncomplying IDS items (e.g., lacking concise explanations for non-English documents) should be identified and may be placed in the file but not considered. Examiners indicate considered citations by initials or alternative electronic signature and strike through citations not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of documents submitted as part of applicant’s reply to Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted and relied upon by applicant when replying to an Office action (e.g., affidavits, patents, printed publications) may be considered by the examiner even if they would not meet 37 CFR 1.97/1.98 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration is limited to the portion of the document relied upon as rebuttal evidence; the entirety may not be considered. Such documents need not be processed as IDS items and the record should reflect whether the evidence was considered; marking on PTO/SB/08 is not required for these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: eIDS (electronic IDS) submission and processing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An eIDS may be submitted via Patent Center by entering citation information in an electronic data entry form; an individual eIDS may contain up to 50 U.S. patents/application publications, 50 foreign patent documents, and 50 NPLs. Copies of foreign patents, NPLs, and unpublished U.S. applications not in IFW must be submitted as PDF via Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may file multiple eIDS submissions; if more than one eIDS is needed and a fee under §1.17(p) applies, only a single fee is required if the fee is included with the first eIDS and subsequent submissions explicitly state the fee was paid and are received the same date. eIDS forms will be scanned into the IFW; examiners must consider compliant eIDS and complete/return a copy to applicant. Accurate citation numbers are important since examiners will electronically retrieve documents by number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notation and record of IDS consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must consider citations submitted in conformance with rules and indicate which citations have been considered by initialing adjacent to considered citations or using alternative electronic signature method (stamp: 'All references considered except where lined through').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners will strike through citations not considered. A copy of the reviewed PTO/SB/08 will be returned to applicant with the next communication, and the original will be entered into the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English reference handling in IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS item in a non-English language fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(3)(i) if it does not include a concise explanation of the relevance (as presently understood by the individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-English information that complies with requirements but is in another language will be considered insofar as it is understood on its face (e.g., drawings, chemical formulas). The examiner need not translate references unless necessary; the examiner's consideration is presumed only to the extent gleanable from applicant’s concise statement and any brief translated portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information printed on patent from IDS citations
rubrics_metrics.description: A citation listed on form PTO/SB/08 and considered by the examiner will be printed on the patent; separate paper lists may be printed if in easily captured uniform format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations printed on patent will be distinguished from examiner-cited PTO-892 citations (examiner-cited marked with an asterisk). If applicant does not provide classification information, the citation will be printed without classification. Duplicate listings are printed only once; application numbers listed on PTO/SB/08 will be printed if considered by the examiner.
